title: Sheet behaviour v1 (cross-commons thin-sheet description)
description: A neutral, unit-explicit, derived description of how a thin sheet behaves: paper and board, fabric and felt, foam, thin prints and laminates of them. The platform that owns a material writes it (from its own card, through a keystone mapping rule); any platform's engine may read it. Axis 1 is the material's principal direction: the machine direction of paper, the warp of a woven, the wale of a knit, the print direction of a thin print, the laminate x axis of a stack. Every number carries its provenance (measured / derived / estimated, with a basis), so an engine can say how far to trust it. This schema checks shape and units; physical admissibility (positive-definite stiffness, regime consistency) is hyperobjects_sheet.validate's job. See docs/SHEET_BEHAVIOUR.md.

sheet_behaviour.description: The contract version. Additive changes keep major 1.

units.description: Restated in every document so the numbers never travel without their units. Each value is fixed by this version.

laminate.const: A N/m, B N, D N*m

axis_1.description: What axis 1 is for this material.

source.description: Where the document came from: the owning platform, the card, and the rule that mapped it.

membrane.description: In-plane stiffness per unit width in the principal axes (modulus × thickness, N/m), and the major Poisson ratio nu12 (strain in axis 2 per strain in axis 1 under a load along axis 1).

bending.description: Plate bending stiffness in N·m (moment per unit width per unit curvature). D16 and D26 are optional and default to 0 (an orthotropic sheet in its principal axes); an angle-ply laminate writes them.

crease.description: Crease and plasticity, where they apply (paper, board, foam). crease_length_scale_t is L*/t (the crease hinge length in calipers); crease_yield_deg the spring-back opening after a crease is released; crease_set_rate how fast a held fold sets (0..1); score_factor the yield of a scored line relative to an unscored one (0..1].

regime.description: Which modelling regime an engine should start from. inextensible and stretchy exclude each other; neither means an ordinary extensible sheet. compressible requires the compression block, layered the laminate block, self_folding the self_folding block.

compression.description: Through-thickness behaviour of a compressible sheet (felt, foam): Ez is the thickness-compression modulus in Pa (compressive stress per unit thickness strain, small strain).

self_folding.description: A 4-D sheet that folds itself when triggered: the trigger and the target curvature [k1, k2, k12] in 1/m it relaxes towards.

contact.description: Contact and damping. friction_static and friction_kinetic are Coulomb coefficients against the same material; damping is a dimensionless fraction of critical damping.

laminate.description: Present when regime.layered: the stack and its classical-laminate matrices (hyperobjects_sheet.laminate). coupled is true when B is non-zero, i.e. the stack curls under in-plane load or layer pre-strain.

provenance.description: One entry per number in the document, keyed by its field name (caliper_mm, E1t, D11, crease_yield_deg, Ez, friction_static, target_curvature_1_m, …). measured: the quantity itself was measured or stated by its maker (a unit conversion keeps the status). derived: computed by a stated formula from measured inputs only. estimated: a literature or engineering estimate, or computed from any estimated input.

notes.description: Mapping caveats a reader must see with the numbers (what was assumed, what the card does not record).

material_ref.description: A material owned by another platform, used by reference (RFC: the sheet-behaviour contract, cross-commons). behaviour "sheet" asks the owning card to carry, or map to, a sheet_behaviour document. role and linked are accepted so the sheet commons' manifest shape (an array of {platform, material_slug, role[, linked]}) can adopt behaviour without a second shape.
